haiku-low.q1: A scheduled 02:00 UTC run for run date D, with retries. It extracts orders with updated_at after HWM minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports stay open, so a row can become visible on the replica up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: Its later updated_at puts it in a nightly window; the MERGE replaces the older live row. Late-visible edits are caught by Sunday reconciliation.
haiku-low.q4: Deleted orders are not removed; the delete sets deleted_at and updated_at, so the merge keeps the row with is_deleted true.
haiku-low.q5: It rolls back, keeps data and HWM unchanged, and logs the error. Attempts 1 and 2 retry after 15 minutes; attempt 3 pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: They show the last committed night, which is consistent. A staleness alert is posted to the #data-alerts channel.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation finds it by count and checksum for the creation day, then reloads that whole day from the replica.
haiku-low.q8: A staged row replaces the live row only when its updated_at is later. Same or older updated_at rows are ignored.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in etl_pipeline_state as hwm_updated_at (UTC). Set to the greater of old HWM and largest staged updated_at, in the same transaction as the MERGE, at commit.
haiku-low.q10: The single warehouse transaction that MERGEs, moves the HWM and marks the run log committed. Readers see the previous night until COMMIT.
haiku-low.q11: The failed table is kept for debugging; retries use a new per-attempt table and never read it. Each retry extracts from HWM minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads all rows created that day from the replica, MERGEs them by the same newer-updated_at rule, and leaves the HWM untouched.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts attempt 1 at 02:00 UTC for run date D. It extracts all columns of orders rows on the replica with updated_at later than HWM minus 2 hours (including deleted rows, via deleted_at), in one read-only snapshot query.
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports stay open up to 90 minutes, so the app can make a row visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at time.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a new updated_at, so the next nightly extract (updated_at later than HWM minus 2h) picks it up and the MERGE replaces the live row because its updated_at is later.
sonnet.q4: The app never hard-deletes; it sets deleted_at and updated_at. The change is extracted like any update, staging sets is_deleted true, and the MERGE updates the live row (one row per order, marked is_deleted) rather than removing it.
sonnet.q5: Roll back the attempt's transaction, leave committed data and HWM unchanged, release the lock if held, log the failure and error in etl_run_log, keep the staging table for debugging. If attempt 1 or 2, the next attempt starts 15 minutes later. If attempt 3 fails, page on-call with run date D and the last error. Each attempt has a 50-minute timeout.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 and show the last committed night's data (consistent). The 06:00 staleness check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts (on-call was already paged if attempt 3 failed).
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation: for each creation day in the last 30 days it compares replica and warehouse row count and checksum; the mismatch triggers a reload of that creation day, which brings in that version.
sonnet.q8: The MERGE replaces a live row only when the staged row's updated_at is later; same or older updated_at is ignored. Validation also keeps just one row per order_id (max updated_at) within staging.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse, in the etl_pipeline_state table (hwm_updated_at, UTC). It is set to the greater of H and the largest updated_at among the staged rows (stays at H if the window was empty), inside the same transaction as the MERGE and the committed run-log row, at commit.
sonnet.q10: Each night's load is staged in a separate staging table readers never see, then merged into orders in a single warehouse transaction that commits atomically; readers see the previous night until the commit, and dashboards read committed data only.
sonnet.q11: Each attempt has its own staging table (stg_orders_<D>_attempt<N>), so the retry never reads the failed attempt's staging; the failed one is kept for debugging. The retry extracts the same kind of window: HWM (unchanged) minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads every row created on that creation day (UTC) from the replica, not just changed rows. They are staged and MERGEd with the same updated_at-later rule in one transaction. The HWM is not touched.
